summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with HIV/AIDS, ESRD on hemodialysis, and a history of recurrent infections was admitted for pleuritic chest pain. Initial workup ruled out cardiac, pulmonary, and aortic causes. The pain resolved with analgesics, and an EGD revealed mild gastritis, managed with omeprazole. During admission, she developed coagulase-negative staph bacteremia, likely from her dialysis line, leading to persistent fever despite antibiotics. The line was removed, and a temporary femoral catheter was placed. She later spiked a fever with a transient retrocardiac opacity on X-ray, treated briefly with antibiotics before resolution. HIV management was addressed, with prophylaxis restarted and plans for HAART reinitiation. She improved clinically, completed treatment, and was discharged home with follow-up plans for ID, nephrology, and neurology.
problems: Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter
Staphylococcus infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site, other staphylococcus
Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
